c001.title: The Missing Watch
c001.briefing.summary: During a private exhibition, gallery owner Adrian Vale leaves his engraved silver wristwatch in his desk drawer and goes downstairs to greet guests. When he returns forty minutes later, his office door is locked, nothing has been forced, and the watch is gone. Three members of staff could have had access. Their accounts don't entirely agree.
c001.briefing.objective1: Who most likely took Adrian Vale's watch?
c001.briefing.objective2: How did they get into the office?
c001.person.adrian.name: Adrian Vale
c001.person.marcus.name: Marcus Reed
c001.person.elena.name: Elena Cross
c001.person.thomas.name: Thomas Bell
c001.e01.title: Adrian Vale's statement
c001.e01.body:
Interviewed 21:32.

“I placed the watch in the top drawer of my desk at 20:40. I closed the drawer but didn't lock it. Then I went downstairs to greet our guests. When I returned at 21:20, the office door was locked, but the watch was gone.”

Adrian is certain he didn't lend or move the watch after 20:40. The drawer is undamaged. The office is on the second floor; its windows are fixed panes that don't open.
c001.f01a: Adrian left his engraved silver watch in the unlocked top drawer of his desk at 20:40.
c001.f01b: At 21:20 the office door was locked, nothing had been forced, and the watch was gone.
c001.f01c: The office windows are fixed panes that don't open.
c001.e02.title: Marcus Reed's statement
c001.e02.body:
Interviewed 21:41. Marcus is the gallery manager; access badge M-04, which opens Adrian's office, is assigned to him.

“I was in the print room the whole time, from about 20:45 until 21:15. The exhibition catalogues needed finishing. My access badge stayed clipped to my jacket. I didn't go anywhere near Adrian's office.”
c001.f02a: Marcus says his access badge M-04 stayed clipped to his jacket.
c001.f02b: Marcus says he was in the print room the whole time, from about 20:45 until 21:15.
c001.f02c: Marcus says he didn't go anywhere near Adrian's office.
c001.e03.title: Elena Cross's statement
c001.e03.body:
Interviewed 21:46. Elena's standard staff badge doesn't open Adrian's office.

“I was on the exhibition floor until just before nine, then I prepared labels in the storage room from about 20:55 until around 21:10. A couple of minutes after quarter to nine — the speeches had just started — I saw Marcus go through the staff door to the back stairs, the stairs up to the offices. The print room is the other way. I didn't think anything of it.”
c001.f03a: Elena says she prepared labels in the storage room from about 20:55 until around 21:10.
c001.f03b: Elena says that at about 20:47 she saw Marcus take the back stairs up to the offices, away from the print room.
c001.f03c: Elena's standard staff badge doesn't open Adrian's office.
c001.e04.title: Thomas Bell's statement
c001.e04.body:
Interviewed 21:52.

“I remained at the security desk from 20:30 until 21:15. The emergency office key stayed inside its sealed cabinet. Nobody reported a problem with the office door that evening.”
c001.f04a: Thomas says he stayed at the security desk from 20:30 until 21:15.
c001.f04b: Thomas says the emergency office key stayed in its sealed cabinet.
c001.e05.title: Office access log
c001.e05.body:
Door controller for Adrian Vale's private office. The system was online and time-synchronised all evening. The door locks automatically when it closes.

20:40 — Door closed and locked (Adrian leaves)
20:48 — Badge M-04 (assigned: Marcus Reed) accepted; door unlocked
20:52 — Door closed and locked
21:20 — Badge A-01 (assigned: Adrian Vale) accepted; door unlocked

The log records which badge was used, not who was holding it.
c001.f05a: 20:40 — The office door closed and locked as Adrian left.
c001.f05b: 20:48 — Badge M-04, assigned to Marcus Reed, unlocked Adrian's office.
c001.f05c: 20:52 — The office door closed and locked again.
c001.f05d: 21:20 — Adrian's own badge unlocked the office.
c001.e06.title: Print server report
c001.e06.body:
Print room printer, exhibition catalogue job.

20:46 — Job submitted from Marcus Reed's workstation (in the print room)
20:47 — Printing started
20:56 — Printing finished
21:12 — Pages collected from the tray (collector not recorded)

The printer runs unattended once a job starts.
c001.f06a: 20:46 — The catalogue print job was sent from Marcus's workstation.
c001.f06b: The printer ran unattended from 20:47 to 20:56; nobody had to stay with it.
c001.f06c: 21:12 — The pages were collected; the log doesn't record by whom.
c001.e07.title: Guest's corridor photograph
c001.e07.body:
Taken at 20:51 on a guest's phone. The guest had wandered through an unmarked staff door looking for the cloakroom.

Photo description: the staff corridor outside the private office — a concrete floor, wrapped artworks leaning against the wall, a utility trolley, a door at the far end. A person in a dark suit is walking away from the camera, away from the office end of the corridor. They are backlit and slightly blurred; their face, hair colour and any badge are not visible. Several men at the exhibition wore dark suits, including Adrian and Marcus.
c001.f07a: 20:51 — A person in a dark suit was walking away from the office end of the staff corridor. Their face isn't visible.
c001.e08.title: Security desk record
c001.e08.body:
Security desk log and equipment checks.

Emergency key cabinet: eight keys behind one tamper seal (the office key hangs on hook 2). Seal 007342 checked intact at 20:30 and at 21:15. The cabinet door sensor recorded no opening.

Radio checks: Thomas Bell answered at 20:49 and 21:02.

CCTV covers the public galleries and the main stairwell only. The staff wing — back corridor, print room, storage room and private office — has no cameras.
c001.f08a: Emergency key cabinet seal 007342 was intact at 20:30 and 21:15, and the cabinet sensor recorded no opening.
c001.f08b: Thomas answered radio checks at 20:49 and 21:02.
c001.f08c: CCTV covers only the public galleries and main stairwell; the staff wing has no cameras.
c001.e09.title: Watch recovery
c001.e09.body:
22:05. With Marcus Reed's consent, his belongings are examined.

An engraved silver wristwatch — steel case and bracelet, black dial, date window, ornately engraved bezel — is found inside the zipped inner pocket of Marcus's navy suit jacket. Its engraving matches Adrian Vale's ownership documents.

Asked about the jacket, Marcus says it stayed with him all evening and nobody else handled it.
c001.f09a: Adrian Vale's engraved silver watch was found in the zipped inner pocket of Marcus's jacket at 22:05.
c001.f09b: Marcus says his jacket stayed with him all evening and nobody else handled it.
c001.d01.title: Marcus's badge account is questionable
c001.d01.description: Marcus says he never went near the office, yet his badge M-04 opened it at 20:48. Either Marcus was at the office, or his badge was.
c001.d02.title: The print job is not an alibi
c001.d02.description: The print job only shows that Marcus's workstation sent pages at 20:46. The printer then ran by itself, so nothing places Marcus in the print room at 20:48.
c001.d03.title: Marcus had Adrian's watch
c001.d03.description: The engraved watch found in Marcus's zipped jacket pocket is the watch Adrian left in his desk drawer.
c001.d04.title: Nobody else had badge M-04
c001.d04.description: By Marcus's own account, his badge stayed clipped to his jacket and the jacket never left him. If that's true, nobody else could have used M-04 at 20:48.
c001.d05.title: Someone left the office just before it locked
c001.d05.description: A dark-suited figure was walking away from the office end of the corridor at 20:51, and the office locked at 20:52. The photo doesn't show who it was.
c001.d06.title: Marcus wasn't in the print room the whole time
c001.d06.description: Elena saw Marcus head up the back stairs toward the offices at about 20:47, away from the print room he says he never left.
c001.d07.title: The emergency key wasn't used
c001.d07.description: Thomas says the emergency key stayed in its cabinet, and the intact seal and silent door sensor back him up.
c001.a01.title: Request a consented search of Marcus's belongings
c001.a01.justification: Marcus's badge opened the office at 20:48, and his print-room alibi doesn't cover that moment. Ask Marcus whether he'll agree to a search of his belongings.
c001.c01.question: Who most likely took the watch?
c001.c02.question: How did they get into the office?
c001.hint.r01: Marcus says he never went near the office. Does any record disagree with him?
c001.hint.r02: Marcus offers the catalogue print job as his alibi. What does the print server actually show?
c001.hint.r03: Is the watch from the search the same one Adrian left in his drawer?
c001.hint.r05: Marcus says his badge stayed clipped to his jacket. What does he say about the jacket itself?
c001.resolution:
Marcus Reed took the watch.

He told you he never went near the office, but his badge M-04 unlocked it at 20:48. His alibi was a print job: the server confirms his workstation sent it at 20:46, but the printer then ran unattended, so it never placed him in the print room at 20:48. Those two discrepancies justified asking for a search, and the engraved watch turned up in the zipped pocket of his jacket.

The access log alone only proves which badge was used, not who held it. What closes the gap is Marcus's own account: the badge was clipped to his jacket, and the jacket never left him. By his own words, nobody else could have used M-04.

What remains uncertain: the corridor photograph never identifies anyone, and nothing here is a confession. This is the best-supported reconstruction of the evening, not a courtroom verdict.

Later that night, Marcus admitted to private debts. That explains a motive, but it was never part of the proof.
